content.text:
### Configure Astro Project with Base Path for GitHub Pages

Source: https://github.com/withastro/docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/en/guides/deploy/github.mdx

This Astro configuration snippet sets the `site` and `base` properties within the `defineConfig` object. The `site` property defines the root URL of the deployed project, while `base` specifies a subpath, which is essential when deploying to GitHub Pages under a repository-specific URL.

```js
site: 'https://astronaut.github.io',
        base: '/my-repo',
```

--------------------------------

### Configure Astro Site URL for GitHub Pages Deployment

Source: https://github.com/withastro/docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/en/guides/deploy/github.mdx

Sets the site configuration in astro.config.mjs to specify the GitHub Pages URL where the project will be deployed. The site property must be set to either the user's GitHub Pages URL or the organization's auto-generated URL to ensure Astro generates correct links and assets.

```javascript
import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config'

export default defineConfig({
  site: 'https://astronaut.github.io',
})
```

--------------------------------

### Configure Astro Base Path for GitHub Pages Repository Subdirectory

Source: https://github.com/withastro/docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/en/guides/deploy/github.mdx

Sets the base path in astro.config.mjs when deploying to a repository subdirectory (not a username.github.io repository). The base property should match the repository name with a leading forward slash, ensuring Astro correctly resolves assets and routes relative to the deployment subdirectory.

```javascript
import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config'

export default defineConfig({
  site: 'https://<username>.github.io',
  base: '/my-repo',
})
```

--------------------------------

### Configure Astro Deployment URL and Path

Source: https://github.com/withastro/docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/en/guides/configuring-astro.mdx

This configuration example for `astro.config.mjs` shows how to set the `site`, `base`, and `trailingSlash` options. These settings are essential for correctly generating sitemaps, creating canonical URLs, and managing URL behavior for deployment environments.

```js
import { defineConfig } from "astro/config";

export default defineConfig({
  site: "https://www.example.com",
  base: "/docs",
  trailingSlash: "always"
});
```

--------------------------------

### Configure Astro Site and Base Paths for GitLab Pages

Source: https://github.com/withastro/docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/en/guides/deploy/gitlab.mdx

This Astro configuration sets the `site` and `base` options for deployment to GitLab Pages. The `site` property defines the base URL of the deployed site, typically `https://<username>.gitlab.io`, while `base` specifies the subpath for repository-based deployments, ensuring Astro correctly resolves paths.

```javascript
import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config';

export default defineConfig({
  site: 'https://<username>.gitlab.io',
  base: '/<my-repo>',
  outDir: 'public',
  publicDir: 'static',
});
```

3. **Astro build output**: By default Astro outputs to `dist/` inside the project. For GitHub Pages, we need to configure `outDir` in astro.config.mjs to point to `../../dist/apps/website` (relative to apps/website) to follow Nx conventions, OR keep default and adjust the deploy workflow path.

4. **GitHub Pages base path**: If deploying to `https://4gray.github.io/iptvnator/`, the site needs `base: '/iptvnator/'` in astro.config.mjs. If using a custom domain, base can be `/`.

5. **GitHub Actions workflow**: Should follow existing patterns - use pnpm v10, Node.js 22, consistent with other workflows. Should use the official `actions/deploy-pages` action (modern approach) instead of pushing to gh-pages branch.

6. **Screenshots path**: Screenshots are in the repo root, not in `docs/`. The landing page needs to either copy them to `apps/website/public/` or reference them from GitHub raw URLs.

7. **Tailwind integration**: The monorepo doesn't use Tailwind anywhere currently. Tailwind should be scoped to the website app only (its own tailwind.config inside apps/website).

8. **Duplicate step numbering**: The original plan has two "Step 5" sections.

9. **Keystatic**: This is marked optional. Should be deferred to a follow-up to keep initial scope manageable.

10. **pnpm workspace**: The `pnpm-workspace.yaml` exists. The website app within `apps/` should be automatically included (Nx apps are typically in the workspace).

## Plan Requirements

Design the implementation plan with:
1. Clear step-by-step instructions
2. Correct pnpm commands
3. Proper Astro configuration for Nx monorepo (outDir, base path)
4. GitHub Actions using modern `actions/deploy-pages` approach
5. Proper asset strategy (copy screenshots to public/ vs reference from GitHub)
6. Scoped Tailwind config
7. Content collections setup for blog
8. Landing page sections (hero, features, screenshots, recent posts, download CTA)
9. Verification steps

Keep Keystatic as a separate optional follow-up step, not part of the core plan.

input.content: --- name: website description: | IPTVnator landing page and blog built with Astro + Tailwind CSS. Use when working with: - Website pages, components, or layouts (apps/website/) - Blog posts and content collections (apps/website/src/content/blog/) - Website styling, Tailwind config, or design system - GitHub Pages deployment workflow - Adding new landing page sections or blog features Triggers: "website", "landing page", "blog", "blog post", "astro", "website deployment" --- # IPTVnator Website (Astro + Tailwind CSS) ## Technology Stack - **Framework**: Astro 5 (Static Site Generator) - **Styling**: Tailwind CSS v3 (scoped to website only) - **Content**: Astro Content Collections with Markdown/MDX - **Deployment**: GitHub Pages via `actions/deploy-pages@v4` - **Integration**: Nx monorepo via `nx:run-commands` executor ## Primary Code Locations ``` apps/website/ ├── astro.config.mjs # Astro config (site, base, outDir, integrations) ├── tailwind.config.mjs # Tailwind config (dark-mode-first, brand colors) ├── tsconfig.json # Extends astro/tsconfigs/strict ├── project.json # Nx project (build/serve/preview targets) ├── package.json # Minimal: name, private, type:module ├── public/ │ ├── favicon.ico │ ├── og-image.png # Social sharing image │ └── images/broken-tv.svg # 404 page illustration ├── src/ │ ├── content.config.ts # Blog collection schema (title, description, pubDate, tags, etc.) │ ├── content/blog/ # Markdown blog posts │ ├── styles/global.css # Tailwind directives + dark mode base styles │ ├── assets/ │ │ ├── logo.png # App icon (256x256) │ │ └── screenshots/ # App screenshots (optimized by Astro ) │ ├── components/ │ │ ├── BaseHead.astro # meta, OG tags, font preloads │ │ ├── Header.astro # Glassmorphism nav with mobile menu │ │ ├── Footer.astro # Social links, license │ │ ├── Hero.astro # Hero section with CTAs and badges │ │ ├── FeatureGrid.astro # Bento-style feature cards │ │ ├── ScreenshotShowcase.astro # Tabbed screenshot gallery │ │ ├── DownloadCTA.astro # Platform download buttons │ │ └── BlogPostCard.astro # Blog post preview card │ ├── layouts/ │ │ ├── BaseLayout.astro # HTML shell (BaseHead + Header + Footer) │ │ └── BlogPost.astro # Blog post layout with author, date, back link │ └── pages/ │ ├── index.astro # Landing page (Hero, Features, Screenshots, Download, Blog) │ ├── blog/index.astro # Blog listing │ ├── blog/[...slug].astro # Dynamic blog post pages │ └── 404.astro # Custom 404 ``` ## Commands ```bash # Development pnpm serve:website # Dev server at http://localhost:4321/iptvnator/ nx serve website # Same thing # Build pnpm build:website # Output to dist/apps/website/ nx build website # Same thing (with Nx caching) # Preview built site nx preview website # Serve built output on port 4322 ``` ## Key Configuration ### Base Path The site deploys to `https://4gray.github.io/iptvnator/`, so: - `astro.config.mjs` has `base: '/iptvnator'` - All internal links must include the base: `href="/iptvnator/blog/"` - Dev server URL: `http://localhost:4321/iptvnator/` - Assets in `public/` are served at `/iptvnator/` ### Build Output - `outDir: '../../dist/apps/website'` in astro.config.mjs - Matches `outputs` in project.json for Nx caching - GitHub Actions uploads from `dist/apps/website` ### Image Optimization Screenshots are in `src/assets/screenshots/` (NOT `public/`). Astro's `` component auto-generates optimized WebP: ```astro --- import { Image } from 'astro:assets'; import heroImg from '../assets/screenshots/hero-dark.png'; --- ``` ## Adding a Blog Post 1. Create `apps/website/src/content/blog/.md` 2. Add frontmatter: ```yaml --- title: 'Post Title' description: 'Short description for previews and SEO.' pubDate: 2025-03-01 author: '4gray' tags: ['release', 'tutorial'] # Optional draft: false # Optional, defaults to false --- ``` 3. Write content in Markdown. The post appears at `/iptvnator/blog//` 4. Draft posts (`draft: true`) are excluded from listing and static paths ## Design System - **Dark mode first**: `bg-slate-950` background, `text-slate-100` text - **Brand color**: Blue palette (`brand-50` to `brand-950`) from tailwind.config.mjs - **Fonts**: Inter (sans) + JetBrains Mono (code) - **Effects**: Glassmorphism header (`backdrop-blur-xl`), gradient glows, subtle border hover states - **Components**: Bento grid cards with `border-white/5 bg-white/[0.02]` pattern ## GitHub Actions Deployment Workflow: `.github/workflows/deploy-website.yml` - Triggers on push to `master` when `apps/website/**` changes - Uses pnpm v10 + Node.js 22 (matches other CI workflows) - Deploys via `actions/deploy-pages@v4` - Requires repo Settings > Pages > Source = "GitHub Actions" ## Adding a New Landing Page Section 1. Create `apps/website/src/components/NewSection.astro` 2. Follow the existing pattern (section > max-w-7xl container > content) 3. Import and add to `src/pages/index.astro` between existing sections 4. Use Tailwind classes from the design system above ## Common Patterns ### Internal links always include base path ```astro Blog ``` ### Static assets in public/ use base path ```astro ``` ### Content collection queries ```astro --- import { getCollection } from 'astro:content'; const posts = (await getCollection('blog')) .filter((post) => !post.data.draft) .sort((a, b) => b.data.pubDate.valueOf() - a.data.pubDate.valueOf()); --- ```

Technology Stack - **Framework**: Astro 5 (Static Site Generator) - **Styling**: Tailwind CSS v3 (scoped to website only) - **Content**: Astro Content Collections with Markdown/MDX - **Deployment**: GitHub Pages via `actions/deploy-pages@v4` - **Integration**: Nx monorepo via `nx:run-commands` executor ## Primary Code Locations ``` apps/website/ ├── astro.config.mjs # Astro config (site, base, outDir, integrations) ├── tailwind.config.mjs # Tailwind config (dark-mode-first, brand colors) ├── tsconfig.json # Extends astro/tsconfigs/strict ├── project.json # Nx project (build/serve/preview targets) ├── package.json # Minimal: name, private, type:module ├── public/ │ ├── favicon.ico │ ├── og-image.png # Social sharing image │ └── images/broken-tv.svg # 404 page illustration ├── src/ │ ├── content.config.ts # Blog collection schema (title, description, pubDate, tags, etc.) │ ├── content/blog/ # Markdown blog posts │ ├── styles/global.css # Tailwind directives + dark mode base styles │ ├── assets/ │ │ ├── logo.png # App icon (256x256) │ │ └── screenshots/ # App screenshots (optimized by Astro ) │ ├── components/ │ │ ├── BaseHead.astro # meta, OG tags, font preloads │ │ ├── Header.astro # Glassmorphism nav with mobile menu │ │ ├── Footer.astro # Social links, license │ │ ├── Hero.astro # Hero section with CTAs and badges │ │ ├── FeatureGrid.astro # Bento-style feature cards │ │ ├── ScreenshotShowcase.astro # Tabbed screenshot gallery │ │ ├── DownloadCTA.astro # Platform download buttons │ │ └── BlogPostCard.astro # Blog post preview card │ ├── layouts/ │ │ ├── BaseLayout.astro # HTML shell (BaseHead + Header + Footer) │ │ └── BlogPost.astro # Blog post layout with author, date, back link │ └── pages/ │ ├── index.astro # Landing page (Hero, Features, Screenshots, Download, Blog) │ ├── blog/index.astro # Blog listing │ ├── blog/[...slug].astro # Dynamic blog post pages │ └── 404.astro # Custom 404 ``` ## Commands ```bash # Development pnpm serve:website # Dev server at http://localhost:4321/iptvnator/ nx serve website # Same thing # Build pnpm build:website # Output to dist/apps/website/ nx build website # Same thing (with Nx caching) # Preview built site nx preview website # Serve built output on port 4322 ``` ## Key Configuration ### Base Path The site deploys to `https://4gray.github.io/iptvnator/`, so: - `astro.config.mjs` has `base: '/iptvnator'` - All internal links must include the base: `href="/iptvnator/blog/"` - Dev server URL: `http://localhost:4321/iptvnator/` - Assets in `public/` are served at `/iptvnator/` ### Build Output - `outDir: '../../dist/apps/website'` in astro.config.mjs - Matches `outputs` in project.json for Nx caching - GitHub Actions uploads from `dist/apps/website` ### Image Optimization Screenshots are in `src/assets/screenshots/` (NOT `public/`). Astro's `` component auto-generates optimized WebP: ```astro --- import { Image } from 'astro:assets'; import heroImg from '../assets/screenshots/hero-dark.png'; --- ``` ## Adding a Blog Post 1. Create `apps/website/src/content/blog/.md` 2. Add frontmatter: ```yaml --- title: 'Post Title' description: 'Short description for previews and SEO.' pubDate: 2025-03-01 author: '4gray' tags: ['release', 'tutorial'] # Optional draft: false # Optional, defaults to false --- ``` 3. Write content in Markdown. The post appears at `/iptvnator/blog//` 4. Draft posts (`draft: true`) are excluded from listing and static paths ## Design System - **Dark mode first**: `bg-slate-950` background, `text-slate-100` text - **Brand color**: Blue palette (`brand-50` to `brand-950`) from tailwind.config.mjs - **Fonts**: Inter (sans) + JetBrains Mono (code) - **Effects**: Glassmorphism header (`backdrop-blur-xl`), gradient glows, subtle border hover states - **Components**: Bento grid cards with `border-white/5 bg-white/[0.02]` pattern ## GitHub Actions Deployment Workflow: `.github/workflows/deploy-website.yml` - Triggers on push to `master` when `apps/website/**` changes - Uses pnpm v10 + Node.js 22 (matches other CI workflows) - Deploys via `actions/deploy-pages@v4` - Requires repo Settings > Pages > Source = "GitHub Actions" ## Adding a New Landing Page Section 1. Create `apps/website/src/components/NewSection.astro` 2. Follow the existing pattern (section > max-w-7xl container > content) 3. Import and add to `src/pages/index.astro` between existing sections 4. Use Tailwind classes from the design system above ## Common Patterns ### Internal links always include base path ```astro Blog ``` ### Static assets in public/ use base path ```astro ``` ### Content collection queries ```astro --- import { getCollection } from 'astro:content'; const posts = (await getCollection('blog')) .filter((post) => !post.data.draft) .sort((a, b) => b.data.pubDate.valueOf() - a.data.pubDate.valueOf()); --- ```

# IPTVnator Website - Getting Started > **Note**: This file is a temporary first-start guide. Remove it once you're familiar with the setup. ## Prerequisites - Node.js 22+ - pnpm 10+ ## Quick Start ```bash # Install dependencies (from repo root) pnpm install # Start the dev server pnpm serve:website ``` Open **http://localhost:4321/iptvnator/** in your browser. > The `/iptvnator/` prefix is required because the site deploys to GitHub Pages at `https://4gray.github.io/iptvnator/`. ## Available Commands | Command | Description | |---------|-------------| | `pnpm serve:website` | Start dev server on port 4321 | | `pnpm build:website` | Build to `dist/apps/website/` | | `nx preview website` | Preview the built site on port 4322 | | `nx build website` | Same as build, with Nx caching | ## Writing a Blog Post 1. Create a new file at `apps/website/src/content/blog/my-post.md` 2. Add the required frontmatter: ```yaml --- title: 'My Post Title' description: 'A short summary for previews and SEO.' pubDate: 2025-02-14 author: '4gray' tags: ['release'] --- ``` 3. Write your content in Markdown below the frontmatter 4. The post will appear at `/iptvnator/blog/my-post/` Set `draft: true` in frontmatter to hide a post from listings while you work on it. ## Project Structure ``` apps/website/ ├── astro.config.mjs # Site URL, base path, integrations ├── tailwind.config.mjs # Colors, fonts (scoped to website) ├── project.json # Nx targets (build, serve, preview) ├── public/ # Static files (served as-is) │ ├── favicon.ico │ ├── og-image.png │ └── images/ ├── src/ │ ├── content.config.ts # Blog collection schema │ ├── content/blog/ # Blog posts (Markdown/MDX) │ ├── styles/global.css # Tailwind + base styles │ ├── assets/ # Images optimized by Astro at build time │ ├── components/ # Reusable Astro components │ ├── layouts/ # Page layout templates │ └── pages/ # File-based routing ``` ## Deploying to GitHub Pages Deployment is automatic via GitHub Actions when you push to `master` and changes exist in `apps/website/`. ### First-time setup (one-time) 1. Go to your GitHub repo **Settings > Pages** 2. Under **Source**, select **"GitHub Actions"** (not "Deploy from a branch") 3. Push a change to `apps/website/` on `master` 4. The site will be live at `https://4gray.github.io/iptvnator/` You can also trigger a manual deploy from the Actions tab using "workflow_dispatch". ## Adding a New Section to the Landing Page 1. Create a component: `src/components/MySection.astro` 2. Import it in `src/pages/index.astro` 3. Add it between existing sections Example: ```astro --- // src/components/MySection.astro ---

My Section

``` ## Design Notes - **Dark mode by default** - the `` tag has `class="dark"` - **Brand color**: Blue (`brand-500` = `#3b82f6`) - defined in `tailwind.config.mjs` - **Fonts**: Inter (body) + JetBrains Mono (code) - **Card pattern**: `rounded-xl border border-white/5 bg-white/[0.02]` with `hover:border-white/10 hover:bg-white/[0.04]` ## Useful Links - [Astro Docs](https://docs.astro.build) - [Tailwind CSS Docs](https://tailwindcss.com/docs) - [Astro Content Collections](https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/content-collections/)

This skill guides creation of distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces that avoid generic "AI slop" aesthetics. Implement real working code with exceptional attention to aesthetic details and creative choices.

The user provides frontend requirements: a component, page, application, or interface to build. They may include context about the purpose, audience, or technical constraints.

## Design Thinking

Before coding, understand the context and commit to a BOLD aesthetic direction:
- **Purpose**: What problem does this interface solve? Who uses it?
- **Tone**: Pick an extreme: brutally minimal, maximalist chaos, retro-futuristic, organic/natural, luxury/refined, playful/toy-like, editorial/magazine, brutalist/raw, art deco/geometric, soft/pastel, industrial/utilitarian, etc. There are so many flavors to choose from. Use these for inspiration but design one that is true to the aesthetic direction.
- **Constraints**: Technical requirements (framework, performance, accessibility).
- **Differentiation**: What makes this UNFORGETTABLE? What's the one thing someone will remember?

**CRITICAL**: Choose a clear conceptual direction and execute it with precision. Bold maximalism and refined minimalism both work - the key is intentionality, not intensity.

Then implement working code (HTML/CSS/JS, React, Vue, etc.) that is:
- Production-grade and functional
- Visually striking and memorable
- Cohesive with a clear aesthetic point-of-view
- Meticulously refined in every detail

## Frontend Aesthetics Guidelines

Focus on:
- **Typography**: Choose fonts that are beautiful, unique, and interesting. Avoid generic fonts like Arial and Inter; opt instead for distinctive choices that elevate the frontend's aesthetics; unexpected, characterful font choices. Pair a distinctive display font with a refined body font.
- **Color & Theme**: Commit to a cohesive aesthetic. Use CSS variables for consistency. Dominant colors with sharp accents outperform timid, evenly-distributed palettes.
- **Motion**: Use animations for effects and micro-interactions. Prioritize CSS-only solutions for HTML. Use Motion library for React when available. Focus on high-impact moments: one well-orchestrated page load with staggered reveals (animation-delay) creates more delight than scattered micro-interactions. Use scroll-triggering and hover states that surprise.
- **Spatial Composition**: Unexpected layouts. Asymmetry. Overlap. Diagonal flow. Grid-breaking elements. Generous negative space OR controlled density.
- **Backgrounds & Visual Details**: Create atmosphere and depth rather than defaulting to solid colors. Add contextual effects and textures that match the overall aesthetic. Apply creative forms like gradient meshes, noise textures, geometric patterns, layered transparencies, dramatic shadows, decorative borders, custom cursors, and grain overlays.

NEVER use generic AI-generated aesthetics like overused font families (Inter, Roboto, Arial, system fonts), cliched color schemes (particularly purple gradients on white backgrounds), predictable layouts and component patterns, and cookie-cutter design that lacks context-specific character.

Interpret creatively and make unexpected choices that feel genuinely designed for the context. No design should be the same. Vary between light and dark themes, different fonts, different aesthetics. NEVER converge on common choices (Space Grotesk, for example) across generations.

**IMPORTANT**: Match implementation complexity to the aesthetic vision. Maximalist designs need elaborate code with extensive animations and effects. Minimalist or refined designs need restraint, precision, and careful attention to spacing, typography, and subtle details. Elegance comes from executing the vision well.

Remember: Claude is capable of extraordinary creative work. Don't hold back, show what can truly be created when thinking outside the box and committing fully to a distinctive vision.

Now I have a thorough understanding of GitButler's design language. Let me plan the redesign and execute it.

**GitButler's key design traits:**
- Custom serif display font ("But Head") with italic emphasis for personality
- Dark, warm background (~`#1c1917`) not cold slate
- Feature cards with dotted/dashed borders, not solid
- Generous whitespace, editorial-like typography
- Mix of serif headlines + sans-serif body (Inter)
- Teal/green accent color, warm palette
- Large product screenshots with subtle window chrome
- Monospace font (Geist Mono) for code/technical details

For IPTVnator, I'll create a distinctive identity inspired by these principles but unique - using a cinematic/broadcast aesthetic befitting a TV/video player.

interface Props {
  title: string;
  description: string;
  image?: string;
}

const canonicalURL = new URL(Astro.url.pathname, Astro.site);
const { title, description, image = '/iptvnator/og-image.png' } = Astro.props;

<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
<link rel="icon" type="image/x-icon" href="/iptvnator/favicon.ico" />
<meta name="generator" content={Astro.generator} />

<!-- Fonts -->
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com" />
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin />
<link
  href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;500;600;700;800&family=JetBrains+Mono:wght@400;500&display=swap"
  rel="stylesheet"
/>

<!-- Canonical URL -->
<link rel="canonical" href={canonicalURL} />

<!-- Primary Meta Tags -->
<title>{title}</title>
<meta name="title" content={title} />
<meta name="description" content={description} />

<!-- Open Graph / Facebook -->
<meta property="og:type" content="website" />
<meta property="og:url" content={Astro.url} />
<meta property="og:title" content={title} />
<meta property="og:description" content={description} />
<meta property="og:image" content={new URL(image, Astro.url)} />

<!-- Twitter -->
<meta property="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image" />
<meta property="twitter:url" content={Astro.url} />
<meta property="twitter:title" content={title} />
<meta property="twitter:description" content={description} />
<meta property="twitter:image" content={new URL(image, Astro.url)} />

The full redesign is complete and the build passes. Here's a summary of what was changed:

## Design System: "Cinematic Broadcast"

**Aesthetic direction** inspired by GitButler - editorial typography, warm dark surfaces, teal accent, dashed borders, monospace labels.

### Typography
- **Display**: Playfair Display (serif with italic emphasis for headlines)
- **Body**: DM Sans (clean, refined sans-serif)

### 3. **Current Interactivity Implementation**

The website uses **vanilla JavaScript embedded in `<script>` tags** within `.astro` files:

#### **ScreenshotShowcase.astro** (Lines 98-128)
- Tab switching functionality with click handlers
- DOM manipulation using `document.querySelectorAll()`
- Class toggling for active/inactive states

#### **Header.astro** (Lines 118-147)

- Header scroll effect with dynamic class management

#### **FeatureGrid.astro**

### 4. **Dependencies Analysis**

From `apps/website/package.json`:
- **Minimal dependencies** - only `astro`, `@astrojs/tailwind`, `@astrojs/sitemap`, `@astrojs/mdx`
- No JavaScript framework dependencies (no React, Vue, Svelte, etc.)
- The website is lightweight with zero client-side framework overhead

### 5. **Architecture Summary**

**Current Approach:**
- Pure Astro static site generation
- Vanilla JavaScript for all interactivity
- No component islands
- All JS runs on the main thread with DOM queries
- Simple, lightweight implementation (~1-2KB of script per feature)

**What's Working:**
- Tab switching (screenshots)
- Copy button (download commands)
- Mobile menu toggle
- Scroll-based header effects

### 6. **Potential Considerations**

**Current Limitations:**
- As the website grows, managing vanilla JS across many interactive components could become harder to maintain
- No state management or component lifecycle
- Scaling interactivity without a framework may become complex
- Each interactive component re-queries the DOM

**If Islands Were Introduced:**
- Could use `@astrojs/react`, `@astrojs/preact`, or `@astrojs/svelte`
- Would enable `client:load`, `client:visible`, `client:idle` directives
- Would allow component-based state management
- Could improve code organization as interactivity increases

### Conclusion

The IPTVnator website takes a **minimalist approach** - it's a pure Astro static site with vanilla JavaScript for light interactivity. **It is NOT currently using Astro's island architecture at all.** This is appropriate for the current level of interactivity (tab switching, copy buttons, mobile menu), but if future requirements demand more complex interactive features, integrating a UI framework with islands would be a logical next step.

Design an implementation plan for enhancing the IPTVnator website blog with thumbnails, a GitButler-inspired grid layout, a new example blog post, and Astro islands for the FeatureGrid.

## Context from exploration

### Current State
The website is at `/Users/4gray/Code/iptvnator/.claude/worktrees/dazzling-lamport/apps/website/`

**Content Schema** (`src/content.config.ts`):
- Already has `heroImage: z.string().optional()` field defined
- Other fields: title, description, pubDate, updatedDate, author, tags, draft

**BlogPostCard** (`src/components/BlogPostCard.astro`):
- Currently takes: title, description, pubDate, slug, tags
- NO image rendering - just text-based card with `card-dotted` class
- Uses font-display for title, font-mono for dates, accent colors

**BlogPost Layout** (`src/layouts/BlogPost.astro`):
- Does NOT receive or render heroImage
- Shows back link, metadata, title, author, divider, then content

**Blog pages**:
- `src/pages/blog/index.astro` - simple vertical list with max-w-2xl, doesn't pass heroImage
- `src/pages/blog/[...slug].astro` - generates static pages, doesn't pass heroImage
- `src/pages/index.astro` - shows latest 3 posts in a 3-col grid on landing page

**Existing blog post** (`src/content/blog/welcome.md`):
- No heroImage field used

**Assets available**: Screenshots in `src/assets/screenshots/` (hero-dark.png, epg.png, player.png, playlists.png, settings.png, upload-file.png, upload-url.png), logo.png

### GitButler Blog Layout Analysis
From Chrome screenshots and JS analysis of https://blog.gitbutler.com/:

1. **Featured post (hero)**: First post is large - 2-column layout. Left: big thumbnail image (rounded corners). Right: metadata + large serif title + description. Full width.

2. **Two-article row**: Next row has 2 posts side by side. Each has: small square thumbnail on left, title + metadata on right. Grid: `2 equal columns, gap 32px`.

3. **Three-column grid** (`post-grid` class): Equal 3-column grid (`378px 378px 378px`, gap `32px`). Each card: thumbnail on top (rounded, colorful), title in serif below, date + author, description.

4. Every post has a colorful custom thumbnail image.
5. Dark background (#1c1917ish), serif titles, warm aesthetic.

### Astro Islands Status
- Currently NO UI framework integrations (no @astrojs/react, preact, svelte)
- NO `client:` directives used anywhere
- Interactive features use vanilla `<script>` tags: ScreenshotShowcase (tabs), DownloadCTA (copy), Header (scroll/mobile menu)
- FeatureGrid has NO interactivity - just static cards with CSS stagger animation
- `astro.config.mjs` integrations: tailwind, sitemap, mdx

### Design System
Warm dark surfaces (#0a0a08 base), teal accent (#20a8a8), Playfair Display serif, DM Sans body, IBM Plex Mono, dashed borders, card-dotted class, section-divider class, stagger-children animation class.

## Requirements

1. **Blog thumbnails**: Wire up the existing `heroImage` schema field through all components:
   - BlogPostCard should display thumbnail image
   - BlogPost layout should show hero image at top of article
   - Blog index page and landing page blog section should pass heroImage
   - Blog slug page should pass heroImage to layout

2. **GitButler-inspired blog grid layout**: Redesign the blog index page:
   - First post: featured/hero style (large, 2-column like GitButler)
   - Remaining posts: 3-column card grid with thumbnails on top
   - Each card has thumbnail, then title, date, description below
   - Match the IPTVnator design system (dashed borders, warm dark, teal accent)
   - Also update the "Latest updates" section on the landing page index.astro

3. **New example blog post**: Create a second `.md` blog entry with a heroImage set. Use one of the existing screenshots as the thumbnail (e.g., `../../assets/screenshots/epg.png`).

4. **Astro islands for FeatureGrid**: 
   - The user asked if "island concept from Astro is used for features"
   - Currently FeatureGrid is fully static with CSS animations
   - We could add a lightweight island for intersection-observer-based stagger (reveal on scroll) instead of CSS-only animations
   - Need to decide: add @astrojs/preact (lightest framework ~3KB) for a small interactive island, OR use vanilla JS with `<script>` tag + IntersectionObserver (no framework needed, still Astro-idiomatic)
   - Recommendation: Use a vanilla `<script>` with IntersectionObserver to add scroll-triggered stagger animation to the FeatureGrid. This is simpler and more aligned with the current codebase (no framework deps needed). Astro islands with `client:visible` require a UI framework integration.

## Plan the implementation

Provide a step-by-step plan for all 4 items above. Include specific file paths, what changes are needed in each file, and the order of operations. Keep it concise but actionable.

1→# Implementation Plan: IPTVnator Landing Page & Blog (Astro + Nx + GitHub Pages)
     2→
     3→## Context
     4→
     5→IPTVnator needs a public-facing website with a landing page and developer blog. The project is an Nx monorepo (v22.3.3) using pnpm, with Angular 20 frontend and Electron backend. There is no existing website - only the PWA app at `iptvnator.vercel.app`. The website will live at `apps/website` and deploy to GitHub Pages via GitHub Actions.
     6→
     7→**Key corrections from original plan:**
     8→- Use **pnpm** (not npm) throughout - the project uses pnpm v10
     9→- Use `nx:run-commands` executor (not bare `command` keys) matching existing patterns
    10→- Use modern `actions/deploy-pages@v4` (not gh-pages branch push)
    11→- Configure Astro `outDir` to `../../dist/apps/website` to follow Nx conventions
    12→- Set `base: '/iptvnator'` for GitHub Pages subdirectory hosting
    13→- Screenshots are in repo root (not `docs/`) - copy to `src/assets/` for Astro image optimization
    14→- Keystatic CMS deferred to follow-up
    15→
    16→---
    17→
    18→## Step 1: Scaffold Astro Project
    19→
    20→Create `apps/website` with minimal Astro setup.
    21→
    22→```bash
    23→cd apps && pnpm create astro@latest website -- --template minimal --no-install --no-git && cd ..
    24→```
    25→
    26→Install dependencies at workspace root:
    27→```bash
    28→pnpm add -D astro @astrojs/tailwind tailwindcss@3 @astrojs/sitemap @astrojs/mdx sharp
    29→```
    30→
    31→Minimal `apps/website/package.json` (keep only):
    32→```json
    33→{ "name": "website", "private": true, "type": "module" }
    34→```
    35→
    36→Add `.astro` to root `.gitignore` (Astro's cache directory).
    37→
    38→---
    39→
    40→## Step 2: Nx Integration - `apps/website/project.json`
    41→
    42→```json
    43→{
    44→  "name": "website",
    45→  "$schema": "../../node_modules/nx/schemas/project-schema.json",
    46→  "projectType": "application",
    47→  "sourceRoot": "apps/website/src",
    48→  "tags": ["type:website"],
    49→  "targets": {
    50→    "build": {
    51→      "executor": "nx:run-commands",
    52→      "outputs": ["{workspaceRoot}/dist/apps/website"],
    53→      "inputs": ["production", "^production"],
    54→      "options": { "command": "npx astro build", "cwd": "apps/website" }
    55→    },
    56→    "serve": {
    57→      "executor": "nx:run-commands",
    58→      "options": { "command": "npx astro dev --port 4321", "cwd": "apps/website" }
    59→    },
    60→    "preview": {
    61→      "executor": "nx:run-commands",
    62→      "dependsOn": ["build"],
    63→      "options": { "command": "npx astro preview --port 4322", "cwd": "apps/website" }
    64→    }
    65→  }
    66→}
    67→```
    68→
    69→Add to root `package.json` scripts:
    70→```json
    71→"serve:website": "nx serve website",
    72→"build:website": "nx build website"
    73→```
    74→
    75→---
    76→
    77→## Step 3: Astro Configuration - `apps/website/astro.config.mjs`
    78→
    79→```js
    80→import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config';
    81→import tailwind from '@astrojs/tailwind';
    82→import sitemap from '@astrojs/sitemap';
    83→import mdx from '@astrojs/mdx';
    84→
    85→export default defineConfig({
    86→  site: 'https://4gray.github.io',
    87→  base: '/iptvnator',
    88→  outDir: '../../dist/apps/website',
    89→  integrations: [tailwind(), sitemap(), mdx()],
    90→});
    91→```
    92→
    93→Key: `outDir` points to Nx output directory. `base: '/iptvnator'` for GitHub Pages repo subdirectory.
    94→
    95→---
    96→
    97→## Step 4: Tailwind CSS - `apps/website/tailwind.config.mjs`
    98→
    99→Scoped to website only. Dark-mode-first design system:
   100→- `darkMode: 'class'` with dark as default
   101→- Blue-based `brand` palette (aligns with existing Material blue theme)
   102→- `Inter` + `JetBrains Mono` font stack
   103→- Content paths scoped to `./src/**/*.{astro,html,js,md,mdx,ts,tsx}`
   104→
   105→Also create:
   106→- `apps/website/tsconfig.json` - extends `astro/tsconfigs/strict`
   107→- `apps/website/src/styles/global.css` - Tailwind directives + dark mode CSS variables
   108→
   109→---
   110→
   111→## Step 5: Asset Strategy
   112→
   113→**Screenshots** (copy from repo root to `apps/website/src/assets/screenshots/`):
   114→| Source | Destination name |
   115→|--------|-----------------|
   116→| `iptv-dark-theme.png` | `hero-dark.png` |
   117→| `iptv-main.png` | `player.png` |
   118→| `iptv-epg.png` | `epg.png` |
   119→| `playlists.png` | `playlists.png` |
   120→| `iptv-settings.png` | `settings.png` |
   121→| `iptv-upload.png` | `upload-file.png` |
   122→| `upload-via-url.png` | `upload-url.png` |
   123→
   124→Place in `src/assets/` (not `public/`) so Astro's `<Image>` component auto-generates WebP/AVIF.
   125→
   126→**Other assets to copy:**
   127→- `apps/web/src/assets/icons/favicon.ico` -> `apps/website/public/favicon.ico`
   128→- `apps/web/src/assets/icons/favicon.256x256.png` -> `apps/website/src/assets/logo.png`
   129→- `iptv-dark-theme.png` -> `apps/website/public/og-image.png` (stable URL for social sharing)
   130→- `apps/web/src/assets/images/broken-tv.svg` -> `apps/website/public/images/broken-tv.svg` (404 page)
   131→
   132→---
   133→
   134→## Step 6: Content Collections - `apps/website/src/content.config.ts`
   135→
   136→Blog collection with schema: `title`, `description`, `pubDate`, `updatedDate?`, `author`, `heroImage?`, `tags[]`, `draft`.
   137→
   138→Create initial post: `apps/website/src/content/blog/welcome.md`
   139→
   140→---
   141→
   142→## Step 7: Page Structure & Components
   143→
   144→### Directory layout:
   145→```
   146→apps/website/src/
   147→  components/
   148→    BaseHead.astro        # <head> meta, OG tags, font preloads
   149→    Header.astro          # Nav: logo, Features, Blog, GitHub, Download CTA
   150→    Footer.astro          # Social links, license, "Built with Astro"
   151→    Hero.astro            # Headline + CTAs + hero screenshot + badges
   152→    FeatureGrid.astro     # 4-column bento grid of features
   153→    ScreenshotShowcase.astro  # Tabbed screenshot gallery
   154→    DownloadCTA.astro     # Platform download buttons + package managers
   155→    BlogPostCard.astro    # Post preview card
   156→    ThemeToggle.astro     # Dark/light toggle
   157→  layouts/
   158→    BaseLayout.astro      # HTML shell wrapping Header + Footer
   159→    BlogPost.astro        # Post layout with date, author, back link
   160→  pages/
   161→    index.astro           # Landing page composing all sections
   162→    blog/index.astro      # Blog listing (all posts sorted by date)
   163→    blog/[...slug].astro  # Dynamic post pages
   164→    404.astro             # Custom 404 with broken-tv.svg
   165→```
   166→
   167→### Landing page sections (top to bottom):
   168→1. **Hero** - "The open-source IPTV player for everyone" + Download / Try Web App CTAs + hero screenshot with glow effect
   169→2. **Features grid** - 16 features from README in bento-style cards with icons
   170→3. **Screenshot showcase** - Tabbed gallery of key screenshots
   171→4. **Download section** - Platform buttons (macOS/Windows/Linux) + Homebrew/Snap/AUR snippets
   172→5. **Recent blog posts** - Latest 3 posts from content collection
   173→6. **Footer** - GitHub, Telegram, Bluesky, Ko-fi links
   174→
   175→### Design system:
   176→- Dark mode first (`bg-neutral-950`)
   177→- Glassmorphism header (`backdrop-blur-md`)
   178→- Subtle gradient accents (`from-blue-500/10 to-purple-500/10`)
   179→- Bento grid cards with rounded corners and subtle borders
   180→- Inter font, clean sans-serif typography
   181→
   182→---
   183→
   184→## Step 8: GitHub Actions - `.github/workflows/deploy-website.yml`
   185→
   186→```yaml
   187→name: Deploy Website to GitHub Pages
   188→on:
   189→  push:
   190→    branches: [master]
   191→    paths: ['apps/website/**', '.github/workflows/deploy-website.yml']
   192→  workflow_dispatch:
   193→
   194→permissions:
   195→  contents: read
   196→  pages: write
   197→  id-token: write
   198→
   199→concurrency:
   200→  group: 'pages'
   201→  cancel-in-progress: true
   202→
   203→jobs:
   204→  build:
   205→    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
   206→    steps:
   207→      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
   208→      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
   209→        with: { version: 10 }
   210→      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
   211→        with: { node-version: '22', cache: 'pnpm' }
   212→      - run: pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile
   213→      - run: npx nx build website
   214→      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
   215→        with: { path: dist/apps/website }
   216→
   217→  deploy:
   218→    needs: build
   219→    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
   220→    environment:
   221→      name: github-pages
   222→      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
   223→    steps:
   224→      - id: deployment
   225→        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
   226→```
   227→
   228→**Post-deploy**: Repository owner must set Settings > Pages > Source to "GitHub Actions".
   229→
   230→---
   231→
   232→## Step 9 (Optional follow-up): Keystatic CMS
   233→
   234→Deferred. Can be added later by installing `@keystatic/core` + `@keystatic/astro` and creating `keystatic.config.tsx`. Provides a `/keystatic` admin UI for editing blog posts via browser.
   235→
   236→---
   237→
   238→## Files Summary
   239→
   240→### New files (~29 files):
   241→| File | Purpose |
   242→|------|---------|
   243→| `apps/website/project.json` | Nx project config |
   244→| `apps/website/package.json` | Minimal package metadata |
   245→| `apps/website/astro.config.mjs` | Astro configuration |
   246→| `apps/website/tailwind.config.mjs` | Scoped Tailwind config |

# Implementation Plan: IPTVnator Landing Page & Blog (Astro + Nx + GitHub Pages)

## Context

IPTVnator needs a public-facing website with a landing page and developer blog. The project is an Nx monorepo (v22.3.3) using pnpm, with Angular 20 frontend and Electron backend. There is no existing website - only the PWA app at `iptvnator.vercel.app`. The website will live at `apps/website` and deploy to GitHub Pages via GitHub Actions.

**Key corrections from original plan:**
- Use **pnpm** (not npm) throughout - the project uses pnpm v10
- Use `nx:run-commands` executor (not bare `command` keys) matching existing patterns
- Use modern `actions/deploy-pages@v4` (not gh-pages branch push)
- Configure Astro `outDir` to `../../dist/apps/website` to follow Nx conventions
- Set `base: '/iptvnator'` for GitHub Pages subdirectory hosting
- Screenshots are in repo root (not `docs/`) - copy to `src/assets/` for Astro image optimization
- Keystatic CMS deferred to follow-up

---

## Step 1: Scaffold Astro Project

Create `apps/website` with minimal Astro setup.

```bash
cd apps && pnpm create astro@latest website -- --template minimal --no-install --no-git && cd ..
```

Install dependencies at workspace root:
```bash
pnpm add -D astro @astrojs/tailwind tailwindcss@3 @astrojs/sitemap @astrojs/mdx sharp
```

Minimal `apps/website/package.json` (keep only):
```json
{ "name": "website", "private": true, "type": "module" }
```

Add `.astro` to root `.gitignore` (Astro's cache directory).

---

## Step 2: Nx Integration - `apps/website/project.json`

```json
{
  "name": "website",
  "$schema": "../../node_modules/nx/schemas/project-schema.json",
  "projectType": "application",
  "sourceRoot": "apps/website/src",
  "tags": ["type:website"],
  "targets": {
    "build": {
      "executor": "nx:run-commands",
      "outputs": ["{workspaceRoot}/dist/apps/website"],
      "inputs": ["production", "^production"],
      "options": { "command": "npx astro build", "cwd": "apps/website" }
    },
    "serve": {
      "executor": "nx:run-commands",
      "options": { "command": "npx astro dev --port 4321", "cwd": "apps/website" }
    },
    "preview": {
      "executor": "nx:run-commands",
      "dependsOn": ["build"],
      "options": { "command": "npx astro preview --port 4322", "cwd": "apps/website" }
    }
  }
}
```

Add to root `package.json` scripts:
```json
"serve:website": "nx serve website",
"build:website": "nx build website"
```

---

## Step 3: Astro Configuration - `apps/website/astro.config.mjs`

```js
import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config';
import tailwind from '@astrojs/tailwind';
import sitemap from '@astrojs/sitemap';
import mdx from '@astrojs/mdx';

export default defineConfig({
  site: 'https://4gray.github.io',
  base: '/iptvnator',
  outDir: '../../dist/apps/website',
  integrations: [tailwind(), sitemap(), mdx()],
});
```

Key: `outDir` points to Nx output directory. `base: '/iptvnator'` for GitHub Pages repo subdirectory.

---

## Step 4: Tailwind CSS - `apps/website/tailwind.config.mjs`

Scoped to website only. Dark-mode-first design system:
- `darkMode: 'class'` with dark as default
- Blue-based `brand` palette (aligns with existing Material blue theme)
- `Inter` + `JetBrains Mono` font stack
- Content paths scoped to `./src/**/*.{astro,html,js,md,mdx,ts,tsx}`

Also create:
- `apps/website/tsconfig.json` - extends `astro/tsconfigs/strict`
- `apps/website/src/styles/global.css` - Tailwind directives + dark mode CSS variables

---

## Step 5: Asset Strategy

**Screenshots** (copy from repo root to `apps/website/src/assets/screenshots/`):
| Source | Destination name |
|--------|-----------------|
| `iptv-dark-theme.png` | `hero-dark.png` |
| `iptv-main.png` | `player.png` |
| `iptv-epg.png` | `epg.png` |
| `playlists.png` | `playlists.png` |
| `iptv-settings.png` | `settings.png` |
| `iptv-upload.png` | `upload-file.png` |
| `upload-via-url.png` | `upload-url.png` |

Place in `src/assets/` (not `public/`) so Astro's `<Image>` component auto-generates WebP/AVIF.

**Other assets to copy:**
- `apps/web/src/assets/icons/favicon.ico` -> `apps/website/public/favicon.ico`
- `apps/web/src/assets/icons/favicon.256x256.png` -> `apps/website/src/assets/logo.png`
- `iptv-dark-theme.png` -> `apps/website/public/og-image.png` (stable URL for social sharing)
- `apps/web/src/assets/images/broken-tv.svg` -> `apps/website/public/images/broken-tv.svg` (404 page)

---

## Step 6: Content Collections - `apps/website/src/content.config.ts`

Blog collection with schema: `title`, `description`, `pubDate`, `updatedDate?`, `author`, `heroImage?`, `tags[]`, `draft`.

Create initial post: `apps/website/src/content/blog/welcome.md`

---

## Step 7: Page Structure & Components

### Directory layout:
```
apps/website/src/
  components/
    BaseHead.astro        # <head> meta, OG tags, font preloads
    Header.astro          # Nav: logo, Features, Blog, GitHub, Download CTA
    Footer.astro          # Social links, license, "Built with Astro"
    Hero.astro            # Headline + CTAs + hero screenshot + badges
    FeatureGrid.astro     # 4-column bento grid of features
    ScreenshotShowcase.astro  # Tabbed screenshot gallery
    DownloadCTA.astro     # Platform download buttons + package managers
    BlogPostCard.astro    # Post preview card
    ThemeToggle.astro     # Dark/light toggle
  layouts/
    BaseLayout.astro      # HTML shell wrapping Header + Footer
    BlogPost.astro        # Post layout with date, author, back link
  pages/
    index.astro           # Landing page composing all sections
    blog/index.astro      # Blog listing (all posts sorted by date)
    blog/[...slug].astro  # Dynamic post pages
    404.astro             # Custom 404 with broken-tv.svg
```

### Landing page sections (top to bottom):
1. **Hero** - "The open-source IPTV player for everyone" + Download / Try Web App CTAs + hero screenshot with glow effect
2. **Features grid** - 16 features from README in bento-style cards with icons
3. **Screenshot showcase** - Tabbed gallery of key screenshots
4. **Download section** - Platform buttons (macOS/Windows/Linux) + Homebrew/Snap/AUR snippets
5. **Recent blog posts** - Latest 3 posts from content collection
6. **Footer** - GitHub, Telegram, Bluesky, Ko-fi links

### Design system:
- Dark mode first (`bg-neutral-950`)
- Glassmorphism header (`backdrop-blur-md`)
- Subtle gradient accents (`from-blue-500/10 to-purple-500/10`)
- Bento grid cards with rounded corners and subtle borders
- Inter font, clean sans-serif typography

---

## Step 8: GitHub Actions - `.github/workflows/deploy-website.yml`

```yaml
name: Deploy Website to GitHub Pages
on:
  push:
    branches: [master]
    paths: ['apps/website/**', '.github/workflows/deploy-website.yml']
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: 'pages'
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with: { version: 10 }
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '22', cache: 'pnpm' }
      - run: pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile
      - run: npx nx build website
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with: { path: dist/apps/website }

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
```

**Post-deploy**: Repository owner must set Settings > Pages > Source to "GitHub Actions".

---

## Step 9 (Optional follow-up): Keystatic CMS

Deferred. Can be added later by installing `@keystatic/core` + `@keystatic/astro` and creating `keystatic.config.tsx`. Provides a `/keystatic` admin UI for editing blog posts via browser.

---

## Files Summary

### New files (~29 files):
| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `apps/website/project.json` | Nx project config |
| `apps/website/package.json` | Minimal package metadata |
| `apps/website/astro.config.mjs` | Astro configuration |
| `apps/website/tailwind.config.mjs` | Scoped Tailwind config |
| `apps/website/tsconfig.json` | TypeScript config |
| `apps/website/src/content.config.ts` | Blog collection schema |
| `apps/website/src/styles/global.css` | Tailwind directives |
| `apps/website/src/components/*.astro` | 8 components (BaseHead, Header, Footer, Hero, FeatureGrid, ScreenshotShowcase, DownloadCTA, BlogPostCard, ThemeToggle) |
| `apps/website/src/layouts/*.astro` | 2 layouts (Base, BlogPost) |
| `apps/website/src/pages/*.astro` | 4 pages (index, blog/index, blog/[...slug], 404) |
| `apps/website/src/content/blog/welcome.md` | First blog post |
| `apps/website/src/assets/` | Logo + 7 screenshots |
| `apps/website/public/` | favicon.ico, og-image.png, broken-tv.svg |
| `.github/workflows/deploy-website.yml` | GitHub Pages deployment |

### Modified files:
| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `package.json` | Add `serve:website`, `build:website` scripts |
| `.gitignore` | Add `.astro` entry |

---

## Verification

1. `pnpm serve:website` -> opens at `http://localhost:4321/iptvnator/`
2. `pnpm build:website` -> output in `dist/apps/website/` with `index.html`
3. `npx nx graph` -> `website` project visible, no dependencies on other projects
4. `npx nx build website` (run twice) -> second run is cached
5. Navigate to `/iptvnator/blog/` -> welcome post renders correctly
6. Check DevTools Network -> screenshots served as optimized WebP/AVIF
7. After merge to master -> GitHub Actions deploys to `https://4gray.github.io/iptvnator/`

cd apps && pnpm create astro@latest website -- --template minimal --no-install --no-git && cd ..
```

Install dependencies at workspace root:
```bash
pnpm add -D astro @astrojs/tailwind tailwindcss@3 @astrojs/sitemap @astrojs/mdx sharp
```

Minimal `apps/website/package.json` (keep only):
```json
{ "name": "website", "private": true, "type": "module" }
```

Add `.astro` to root `.gitignore` (Astro's cache directory).

---

## Step 2: Nx Integration - `apps/website/project.json`

```json
{
  "name": "website",
  "$schema": "../../node_modules/nx/schemas/project-schema.json",
  "projectType": "application",
  "sourceRoot": "apps/website/src",
  "tags": ["type:website"],
  "targets": {
    "build": {
      "executor": "nx:run-commands",
      "outputs": ["{workspaceRoot}/dist/apps/website"],
      "inputs": ["production", "^production"],
      "options": { "command": "npx astro build", "cwd": "apps/website" }
    },
    "serve": {
      "executor": "nx:run-commands",
      "options": { "command": "npx astro dev --port 4321", "cwd": "apps/website" }
    },
    "preview": {
      "executor": "nx:run-commands",
      "dependsOn": ["build"],
      "options": { "command": "npx astro preview --port 4322", "cwd": "apps/website" }
    }
  }
}
```

Add to root `package.json` scripts:
```json
"serve:website": "nx serve website",
"build:website": "nx build website"
```

---

## Step 3: Astro Configuration - `apps/website/astro.config.mjs`

```js
import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config';
import tailwind from '@astrojs/tailwind';
import sitemap from '@astrojs/sitemap';
import mdx from '@astrojs/mdx';

export default defineConfig({
  site: 'https://4gray.github.io',
  base: '/iptvnator',
  outDir: '../../dist/apps/website',
  integrations: [tailwind(), sitemap(), mdx()],
});
```

Key: `outDir` points to Nx output directory. `base: '/iptvnator'` for GitHub Pages repo subdirectory.

---

## Step 4: Tailwind CSS - `apps/website/tailwind.config.mjs`

Scoped to website only. Dark-mode-first design system:
- `darkMode: 'class'` with dark as default
- Blue-based `brand` palette (aligns with existing Material blue theme)
- `Inter` + `JetBrains Mono` font stack
- Content paths scoped to `./src/**/*.{astro,html,js,md,mdx,ts,tsx}`

Also create:
- `apps/website/tsconfig.json` - extends `astro/tsconfigs/strict`
- `apps/website/src/styles/global.css` - Tailwind directives + dark mode CSS variables

---

## Step 5: Asset Strategy

**Screenshots** (copy from repo root to `apps/website/src/assets/screenshots/`):
| Source | Destination name |
|--------|-----------------|
| `iptv-dark-theme.png` | `hero-dark.png` |
| `iptv-main.png` | `player.png` |
| `iptv-epg.png` | `epg.png` |
| `playlists.png` | `playlists.png` |
| `iptv-settings.png` | `settings.png` |
| `iptv-upload.png` | `upload-file.png` |
| `upload-via-url.png` | `upload-url.png` |

Place in `src/assets/` (not `public/`) so Astro's `<Image>` component auto-generates WebP/AVIF.

**Other assets to copy:**
- `apps/web/src/assets/icons/favicon.ico` -> `apps/website/public/favicon.ico`
- `apps/web/src/assets/icons/favicon.256x256.png` -> `apps/website/src/assets/logo.png`
- `iptv-dark-theme.png` -> `apps/website/public/og-image.png` (stable URL for social sharing)
- `apps/web/src/assets/images/broken-tv.svg` -> `apps/website/public/images/broken-tv.svg` (404 page)

---

## Step 6: Content Collections - `apps/website/src/content.config.ts`

Blog collection with schema: `title`, `description`, `pubDate`, `updatedDate?`, `author`, `heroImage?`, `tags[]`, `draft`.

Create initial post: `apps/website/src/content/blog/welcome.md`

---

## Step 7: Page Structure & Components

### Directory layout:
```
apps/website/src/
  components/
    BaseHead.astro        # <head> meta, OG tags, font preloads
    Header.astro          # Nav: logo, Features, Blog, GitHub, Download CTA
    Footer.astro          # Social links, license, "Built with Astro"
    Hero.astro            # Headline + CTAs + hero screenshot + badges
    FeatureGrid.astro     # 4-column bento grid of features
    ScreenshotShowcase.astro  # Tabbed screenshot gallery
    DownloadCTA.astro     # Platform download buttons + package managers
    BlogPostCard.astro    # Post preview card
    ThemeToggle.astro     # Dark/light toggle
  layouts/
    BaseLayout.astro      # HTML shell wrapping Header + Footer
    BlogPost.astro        # Post layout with date, author, back link
  pages/
    index.astro           # Landing page composing all sections
    blog/index.astro      # Blog listing (all posts sorted by date)
    blog/[...slug].astro  # Dynamic post pages
    404.astro             # Custom 404 with broken-tv.svg
```

### Landing page sections (top to bottom):
1. **Hero** - "The open-source IPTV player for everyone" + Download / Try Web App CTAs + hero screenshot with glow effect
2. **Features grid** - 16 features from README in bento-style cards with icons
3. **Screenshot showcase** - Tabbed gallery of key screenshots
4. **Download section** - Platform buttons (macOS/Windows/Linux) + Homebrew/Snap/AUR snippets
5. **Recent blog posts** - Latest 3 posts from content collection
6. **Footer** - GitHub, Telegram, Bluesky, Ko-fi links

### Design system:
- Dark mode first (`bg-neutral-950`)
- Glassmorphism header (`backdrop-blur-md`)
- Subtle gradient accents (`from-blue-500/10 to-purple-500/10`)
- Bento grid cards with rounded corners and subtle borders
- Inter font, clean sans-serif typography

---

## Step 8: GitHub Actions - `.github/workflows/deploy-website.yml`

```yaml
name: Deploy Website to GitHub Pages
on:
  push:
    branches: [master]
    paths: ['apps/website/**', '.github/workflows/deploy-website.yml']
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: 'pages'
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with: { version: 10 }
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '22', cache: 'pnpm' }
      - run: pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile
      - run: npx nx build website
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with: { path: dist/apps/website }

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
```

**Post-deploy**: Repository owner must set Settings > Pages > Source to "GitHub Actions".

---

## Step 9 (Optional follow-up): Keystatic CMS

Deferred. Can be added later by installing `@keystatic/core` + `@keystatic/astro` and creating `keystatic.config.tsx`. Provides a `/keystatic` admin UI for editing blog posts via browser.

---

### New files (~29 files):
| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `apps/website/project.json` | Nx project config |
| `apps/website/package.json` | Minimal package metadata |
| `apps/website/astro.config.mjs` | Astro configuration |
| `apps/website/tailwind.config.mjs` | Scoped Tailwind config |
| `apps/website/tsconfig.json` | TypeScript config |
| `apps/website/src/content.config.ts` | Blog collection schema |
| `apps/website/src/styles/global.css` | Tailwind directives |
| `apps/website/src/components/*.astro` | 8 components (BaseHead, Header, Footer, Hero, FeatureGrid, ScreenshotShowcase, DownloadCTA, BlogPostCard, ThemeToggle) |
| `apps/website/src/layouts/*.astro` | 2 layouts (Base, BlogPost) |
| `apps/website/src/pages/*.astro` | 4 pages (index, blog/index, blog/[...slug], 404) |
| `apps/website/src/content/blog/welcome.md` | First blog post |
| `apps/website/src/assets/` | Logo + 7 screenshots |
| `apps/website/public/` | favicon.ico, og-image.png, broken-tv.svg |
| `.github/workflows/deploy-website.yml` | GitHub Pages deployment |

### Modified files:
| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `package.json` | Add `serve:website`, `build:website` scripts |
| `.gitignore` | Add `.astro` entry |

---

## Verification

1. `pnpm serve:website` -> opens at `http://localhost:4321/iptvnator/`
2. `pnpm build:website` -> output in `dist/apps/website/` with `index.html`
3. `npx nx graph` -> `website` project visible, no dependencies on other projects
4. `npx nx build website` (run twice) -> second run is cached
5. Navigate to `/iptvnator/blog/` -> welcome post renders correctly
6. Check DevTools Network -> screenshots served as optimized WebP/AVIF
7. After merge to master -> GitHub Actions deploys to `https://4gray.github.io/iptvnator/`

---
title: 'Understanding the Electronic Program Guide'
description: 'Learn how IPTVnator uses XMLTV data to display current and upcoming programs alongside your live TV channels.'
pubDate: 2025-02-15
author: '4gray'
heroImage: '/iptvnator/blog/epg.png'
tags: ['tutorial', 'epg']
---

One of the most useful features in IPTVnator is the built-in Electronic Program Guide (EPG). Here is how it works and how to set it up.

## What is EPG?

The Electronic Program Guide displays a schedule of current and upcoming TV programs for your channels. IPTVnator supports EPG data in the **XMLTV format**, which is the standard used by most IPTV providers.

## Setting up EPG

To enable EPG in IPTVnator:

1. **Open your playlist** and navigate to the Settings tab
2. **Add an EPG URL** — your IPTV provider should supply a URL ending in `.xml` or `.xml.gz`
3. **Refresh the EPG data** — IPTVnator will download and parse the program information in the background

The EPG data is parsed in a background worker thread, so it won't slow down the main application even with large files.

## EPG in action

Once configured, you will see:

- **Current program** displayed next to each channel in the channel list
- **Progress bar** showing how far through the current program you are
- **Program details** in the right sidebar when you select a channel
- **Upcoming schedule** with times and descriptions for future programs

## Channel matching

IPTVnator matches EPG data to channels using the `tvg-id` attribute from your M3U playlist. Make sure your playlist includes these IDs for the best EPG experience.

## Tips

- EPG files can be large — IPTVnator caches parsed data in the database (Electron) or IndexedDB (PWA) for faster loading
- You can add multiple EPG sources per playlist
- The EPG automatically refreshes periodically to keep the schedule up to date

---
title: 'Understanding the Electronic Program Guide'
description: 'Learn how IPTVnator uses XMLTV data to display current and upcoming programs alongside your live TV channels.'
pubDate: 2025-02-15
author: '4gray'
heroImage: '/iptvnator/blog/epg.png'
tags: ['tutorial', 'epg']
---

One of the most useful features in IPTVnator is the built-in Electronic Program Guide (EPG). Here is how it works and how to set it up.

## What is EPG?

The Electronic Program Guide displays a schedule of current and upcoming TV programs for your channels. IPTVnator supports EPG data in the **XMLTV format**, which is the standard used by most IPTV providers.

## Setting up EPG

To enable EPG in IPTVnator:

1. **Open your playlist** and navigate to the Settings tab
2. **Add an EPG URL** — your IPTV provider should supply a URL ending in `.xml` or `.xml.gz`
3. **Refresh the EPG data** — IPTVnator will download and parse the program information in the background

The EPG data is parsed in a background worker thread, so it won't slow down the main application even with large files.

## EPG in action

Once configured, you will see:

- **Current program** displayed next to each channel in the channel list
- **Progress bar** showing how far through the current program you are
- **Program details** in the right sidebar when you select a channel
- **Upcoming schedule** with times and descriptions for future programs

## Channel matching

IPTVnator matches EPG data to channels using the `tvg-id` attribute from your M3U playlist. Make sure your playlist includes these IDs for the best EPG experience.

## Tips

- EPG files can be large — IPTVnator caches parsed data in the database (Electron) or IndexedDB (PWA) for faster loading
- You can add multiple EPG sources per playlist
- The EPG automatically refreshes periodically to keep the schedule up to date

Check the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/4gray/iptvnator) for more information on supported EPG formats.

1. **Blog thumbnails** — `heroImage` is now wired through all components:

   - The newest post as a large **featured card** (2-column: thumbnail + content)
   - Remaining posts in a responsive **3-column grid** with thumbnails

4. **Scroll-triggered stagger animation** — The FeatureGrid cards are hidden by default (`opacity-0`) and animate in with a staggered fade-up effect when they scroll into view, using `IntersectionObserver` (vanilla JS, no framework island needed)

     3→description: 'We are excited to launch the official IPTVnator website and developer blog. Stay tuned for release notes, tutorials, and roadmap updates.'

     5→author: '4gray'

     8→
     9→We are excited to launch the official IPTVnator website and developer blog!
    10→
    11→## What is IPTVnator?
    12→
    13→IPTVnator is a free, open-source IPTV player application that supports M3U/M3U8 playlists, Xtream Codes API, and Stalker portals. It runs as a desktop application (via Electron) and as a Progressive Web App directly in your browser.
    14→
    15→## What to expect from this blog
    16→
    17→This blog will be the home for:
    18→
    19→- **Release notes** for new versions
    20→- **Tutorials** on how to get the most out of IPTVnator
    21→- **Roadmap updates** so you know what features are coming next
    22→- **Technical deep dives** into the architecture and development process
    23→
    24→## Get involved
    25→
    26→IPTVnator is open source and we welcome contributions! Check out our [GitHub repository](https://github.com/4gray/iptvnator) to get started.

Build passes. The fix was straightforward — the nav links for "Features", "Screenshots", and "Download" were using bare anchor hrefs like `#features`, which only resolve to sections on the current page. When you're on `/blog/`, there are no such sections, so the links did nothing. 

I changed them to absolute paths (`/iptvnator/#features`, `/iptvnator/#screenshots`, `/iptvnator/#download`) so they always navigate back to the homepage first, then scroll to the correct section.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/4gray/.claude/plugins/cache/anthropic-agent-skills/example-skills/f23222824449/skills/frontend-design

This skill guides creation of distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces that avoid generic "AI slop" aesthetics. Implement real working code with exceptional attention to aesthetic details and creative choices.

The user provides frontend requirements: a component, page, application, or interface to build. They may include context about the purpose, audience, or technical constraints.

## Design Thinking

Before coding, understand the context and commit to a BOLD aesthetic direction:
- **Purpose**: What problem does this interface solve? Who uses it?
- **Tone**: Pick an extreme: brutally minimal, maximalist chaos, retro-futuristic, organic/natural, luxury/refined, playful/toy-like, editorial/magazine, brutalist/raw, art deco/geometric, soft/pastel, industrial/utilitarian, etc. There are so many flavors to choose from. Use these for inspiration but design one that is true to the aesthetic direction.
- **Constraints**: Technical requirements (framework, performance, accessibility).
- **Differentiation**: What makes this UNFORGETTABLE? What's the one thing someone will remember?

**CRITICAL**: Choose a clear conceptual direction and execute it with precision. Bold maximalism and refined minimalism both work - the key is intentionality, not intensity.

Then implement working code (HTML/CSS/JS, React, Vue, etc.) that is:
- Production-grade and functional
- Visually striking and memorable
- Cohesive with a clear aesthetic point-of-view
- Meticulously refined in every detail

## Frontend Aesthetics Guidelines

Focus on:
- **Typography**: Choose fonts that are beautiful, unique, and interesting. Avoid generic fonts like Arial and Inter; opt instead for distinctive choices that elevate the frontend's aesthetics; unexpected, characterful font choices. Pair a distinctive display font with a refined body font.
- **Color & Theme**: Commit to a cohesive aesthetic. Use CSS variables for consistency. Dominant colors with sharp accents outperform timid, evenly-distributed palettes.
- **Motion**: Use animations for effects and micro-interactions. Prioritize CSS-only solutions for HTML. Use Motion library for React when available. Focus on high-impact moments: one well-orchestrated page load with staggered reveals (animation-delay) creates more delight than scattered micro-interactions. Use scroll-triggering and hover states that surprise.
- **Spatial Composition**: Unexpected layouts. Asymmetry. Overlap. Diagonal flow. Grid-breaking elements. Generous negative space OR controlled density.
- **Backgrounds & Visual Details**: Create atmosphere and depth rather than defaulting to solid colors. Add contextual effects and textures that match the overall aesthetic. Apply creative forms like gradient meshes, noise textures, geometric patterns, layered transparencies, dramatic shadows, decorative borders, custom cursors, and grain overlays.

NEVER use generic AI-generated aesthetics like overused font families (Inter, Roboto, Arial, system fonts), cliched color schemes (particularly purple gradients on white backgrounds), predictable layouts and component patterns, and cookie-cutter design that lacks context-specific character.

Interpret creatively and make unexpected choices that feel genuinely designed for the context. No design should be the same. Vary between light and dark themes, different fonts, different aesthetics. NEVER converge on common choices (Space Grotesk, for example) across generations.

**IMPORTANT**: Match implementation complexity to the aesthetic vision. Maximalist designs need elaborate code with extensive animations and effects. Minimalist or refined designs need restraint, precision, and careful attention to spacing, typography, and subtle details. Elegance comes from executing the vision well.

Remember: Claude is capable of extraordinary creative work. Don't hold back, show what can truly be created when thinking outside the box and committing fully to a distinctive vision.


ARGUMENTS: Redesign the download button/CTA on the IPTVnator homepage hero section to be much larger and more prominent like GitButler's website. Add a TV-themed hover effect - think static/noise/scanline animation that fits the "cinematic broadcast" design system. The button should feel special and unique with TV-inspired micro-interactions on hover.
Let me first examine the current Hero component and the design system to understand the existing aesthetic before designing the TV-effect button.

content.text:
Excellent — GitButler's download button is large, uses a serif display font, has a teal/dark-teal gradient, rounded pill shape, and on hover shows animated particle/sparkle effects. Now I have a clear vision for the IPTVnator version.

My design concept: A **massive** hero CTA button with TV static/noise effect on hover. The button will have:
- Large display serif text like GitButler
- A scanline animation that sweeps across on hover
- TV static noise texture that appears on hover 
- A glitch/chromatic aberration text effect on hover
- CRT screen glow bloom around the button

Let me now add the TV-effect animations to the tailwind config and then redesign the Hero buttons:

### TV-Effect Download Button

**Design concept**: A massive, GitButler-scale CTA with a "CRT turning on" hover effect — fitting the cinematic broadcast theme.

**What was built:**

1. **`Hero.astro`** — The small `bg-accent-500` button was replaced with a large `btn-tv` card-style button featuring:

   - Monospace platform sub-label: `macOS · Windows · Linux`
   - Download arrow icon that nudges down on hover
   - Secondary "Or try the Web App →" link below

2. **`global.css`** — New `.btn-tv` component with layered TV effects:
   - **Scanline overlay** (`::before`) — Faint horizontal lines like a CRT screen
   - **Scanline sweep** (`.tv-scanline`) — A light band that continuously scrolls across on hover
   - **Static noise** (`.tv-noise`) — SVG turbulence noise that flickers on hover via `tvFlicker` animation
   - **CRT vignette** (`.tv-vignette`) — Corner darkening like a real CRT tube
   - **Text glitch** (`.btn-tv-text`) — Subtle chromatic aberration (teal/red split) that triggers briefly every ~4 seconds on hover
   - **Glow bloom** — Box-shadow that intensifies from 20px to 100px spread on hover

3. **`tailwind.config.mjs`** — Added `tvScan`, `tvFlicker`, and `tvGlow` keyframes/animations

content.text:
Great! Now let me compile my findings with a comprehensive report. Let me create a summary of all the information gathered.

## Exploration Complete

Based on my thorough examination of the IPTVnator Astro website codebase, here's my detailed report:

### **All 12 Feature Items**

1. **M3U / M3U8 Playlists** - Import playlists from files or URLs with full M3U and M3U8 support.
2. **Xtream Codes API** - Connect to Xtream Codes providers with live TV, VOD, and series.
3. **Stalker Portals** - Browse and stream content from Stalker/Ministra portal providers.
4. **Electronic Program Guide** - XMLTV-based EPG with current and upcoming program information.
5. **Favorites & History** - Mark channels as favorites and keep track of recently watched.
6. **Search & Filter** - Quickly find channels across playlists with full-text search.
7. **Multi-Language** - Available in 16 languages with community-contributed translations.
8. **Cross-Platform** - Runs on macOS, Windows, Linux as a desktop app or PWA in any browser.
9. **External Players** - Open streams in MPV, VLC, or other external players from the app.
10. **Light & Dark Themes** - Choose between light and dark themes for comfortable viewing.
11. **Remote Control** - Control the player from your phone with the built-in remote.
12. **Privacy First** - No tracking, no analytics. Your data stays on your device.

---

### **Most Important / Differentiating Features for IPTV Player**

These stand out as **hero/primary features** (core value propositions):

- **M3U / M3U8 Playlists** (item 1) - Core IPTV functionality
- **Xtream Codes API** (item 2) - Major provider integration
- **Stalker Portals** (item 3) - Premium provider integration
- **Electronic Program Guide** (item 4) - Key viewing experience differentiator
- **Privacy First** (item 12) - Strong competitive advantage vs closed-source players

**Secondary differentiators** for the carousel:

- External Players, Remote Control, Favorites/History, Search, Cross-Platform, Themes, Multi-Language

---

### **Existing Animation & Scroll Patterns**

**In `global.css`:**

1. **Stagger Animation System**:
   - `.stagger-children` - Items start hidden (`opacity-0`)
   - `.stagger-visible` - Applied via IntersectionObserver to trigger animations
   - 12 nth-child delays (0ms to 880ms in 80ms increments)
   - Uses `animate-fade-up` Tailwind animation

2. **Tailwind Animations Configured** (`tailwind.config.mjs`):
   - `fade-up`: Combines opacity and translateY movement (0.8s duration)
   - `fade-in`: Simple opacity (0.6s)
   - `glow-pulse`: Pulsing glow effect (4s)
   - `scan` & `tv-scan`: Vertical scanning effects (8s & 3s)
   - `tv-flicker` & `tv-glow`: CRT monitor effects
   - All use cubic-bezier easing for smooth motion

3. **No existing carousel/slider patterns** - The codebase uses simpler patterns like tab-switching and staggered grids.

---

### **Vanilla JS Interaction Patterns in This Codebase**

All components use Astro's `<script>` tags with vanilla JS (no framework):

**ScreenshotShowcase.astro** (Tab switcher pattern):
- Uses `querySelector` / `querySelectorAll` to find elements
- Event listeners for clicks on tab buttons
- Class manipulation for state: `classList.add()`, `classList.remove()`, `classList.toggle()`
- `dataset` properties to store identifiers
- `setAttribute()` for ARIA attributes
- **Panel switching**: Hide/show with `hidden` class toggle

**DownloadCTA.astro** (Copy-to-clipboard + async feedback):
- One-off event listeners using `forEach()`
- `navigator.clipboard.writeText()` for copy functionality
- SVG innerHTML manipulation for visual feedback
- `setTimeout()` for delayed state reset
- Type casting with `as HTMLElement` (TypeScript in Astro)

**Header.astro** (Scroll tracking + mobile menu):
- `scroll` event listener with throttling via `window.scrollY`
- Conditional class toggling based on scroll position (threshold: 50px)
- Mobile menu toggle with icon swapping
- Multiple class toggling in one go for header effects

---

### **Key Implementation Insights**

1. **No dependencies**: No Swiper, Splide, or carousel libraries - everything is vanilla JS
2. **Event delegation**: Simple one-off listeners per component
3. **Tailwind for animations**: All timing/easing controlled via config
4. **IntersectionObserver**: Used for scroll-triggered stagger animations
5. **CSS transitions**: `transition-all duration-X` for smooth effects
6. **Data attributes**: `data-*` used to identify elements and store small config

---

### **Recommendations for Your Redesign**

For the hero + carousel redesign:

1. **Hero Features Section**:
   - Keep the stagger animation for the 5 hero cards
   - Use a grid layout: 2 columns on desktop, 1 on mobile (or 3-2 split)
   - Larger cards with more prominent iconography

2. **Carousel for Remaining Features**:
   - **Vanilla JS scroll container** with CSS `scroll-snap-type: x mandatory` for snap-to-scroll
   - **Navigation buttons** using querySelector to control scroll position
   - Can use `Element.scrollLeft` and smooth scrolling
   - On mobile: native scroll behavior with touch support (built-in)
   - Optional: IntersectionObserver to detect which card is "active" for indicator dots

3. **Animation Strategy**:
   - Reuse existing `animate-fade-up` for hero cards

HTML Structure The component will be restructured within `apps/website/src/components/FeatureGrid.astro`. The frontmatter splits the 12 features into two arrays. The template renders two sub-sections: Hero grid and Carousel marquee. #### Frontmatter (TypeScript in `---` block) Split features into two arrays: ```typescript const heroFeatures = [ { icon: '...', title: 'M3U / M3U8 Playlists', description: '...' }, { icon: '...', title: 'Xtream Codes API', description: '...' }, { icon: '...', title: 'Electronic Program Guide', description: '...' }, { icon: '...', title: 'Cross-Platform', description: '...' }, ]; const carouselFeatures = [ { icon: '...', title: 'Stalker Portals', description: '...' }, { icon: '...', title: 'Favorites & History', description: '...' }, { icon: '...', title: 'Search & Filter', description: '...' }, { icon: '...', title: 'Multi-Language', description: '...' }, { icon: '...', title: 'External Players', description: '...' }, { icon: '...', title: 'Light & Dark Themes', description: '...' }, { icon: '...', title: 'Remote Control', description: '...' }, { icon: '...', title: 'Privacy First', description: '...' }, ]; ``` The icon SVG paths remain exactly as in the current component. No icon data changes. #### HTML Template Structure ```html

Everything you need

{heroFeatures.map((feature) => (

{feature.title}

{feature.description}

{carouselFeatures.map((feature) => (

{feature.title}
